content.text:
I'm mapping out the grid to find connected components of value-3 cells using diagonal adjacency, listing out each row's positions to prepare for removing isolated singleton cells.

Tracing through the connections, I find groups like {(0,1),(1,0),(2,0)} sized 3, an isolated (0,4) singleton to remove, and a larger component connecting (0,10) through several row-1 cells, plus a small pair {(0,13),(1,13)} - continuing to trace which cells link together to determine what stays and what gets removed.

Continuing to check isolated cells and small pairs: (5,5), (6,0), (6,11), (9,1), (9,13) are all singletons with no adjacent neighbors, so I'm removing them, while (7,4)-(7,5) and (8,10)-(8,11) form isolated pairs that stay.

(10,4) turns out to connect into a larger cluster — tracing through diagonal and orthogonal neighbors links it to (11,3), (11,5), (12,3)-(12,5), (13,3), (13,6), (14,2), and eventually up to (16,6) via (15,5), so I'm mapping out this whole connected chain carefully.

I also spot (12,7),(12,8) merging into the same big component through (13,6), while (14,8) stays isolated with no neighbors and gets dropped, and (13,0),(14,0),(15,0) form their own separate cluster to check.

(13,12) links diagonally to (14,11) forming a size-2 component, (16,2)/(16,3) and (16,12)/(16,13) each stand alone as pairs, and (10,10) has no neighbors so it's removed.

Now I'm starting to assemble the row-by-row output array, marking which columns survive per row.
